solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mentions about sacred chest found in manuscript

indicators.note: something found in a thing sits within it, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: re means about, as in a letter heading
MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript
the Ark of the Covenant was the sacred chest of the Israelites

explanation.surface: Someone notes references to a holy chest turning up in an old handwritten document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentions' reads like a verb, but here it is a plural noun: things said in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks and mentions are both plural nouns for things said in passing about a subject.

clue.text: Affectation of superiority after salesman retires

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the later piece is written second

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
to put on airs is to act superior

explanation.surface: A snooty manner shows itself once the salesman has gone off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is at the end; the long opening phrase is wordplay, written after REP.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal idiom for going there, as when guests withdraw or retire to the drawing room.

clue.text: A cold lake in marshy area? Marvellous thing

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
L is the map abbreviation for lake
a mire is a swamp or bog

explanation.surface: Finding a chilly lake in a bog would be quite a wonder, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the definition follows it as a separate sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a wonderful event or object beyond normal expectation, so a marvel in the broad sense.

clue.text: Provoke arguments on the podcast

indicators.note: a podcast is listened to, so we take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: A podcast host stirs up quarrels to get a reaction from listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Row in the quarrel sense rhymes with now, not with go; that pronunciation is what makes the sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to stir them up or excite them into anger or action.

clue.text: Diet is as arranged, keeping female happy

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a new order, so the fodder is reshuffled
to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
the first word of the indicator phrase also counts as fodder
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A dieter is pleased with how the meal plan has been set out for her.
explanation.walkthrough: DIET IS AS is rearranged into SATIS-IED with F held in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied means content, pleased with how things are, a close synonym of happy.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French leader in Parisian broadcast

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
the opening letter of the word
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A French political leader's televised speech leaves the nation without hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the French gives DES, the plural French article, not DU or DE LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the state of having lost all hope, so it is the noun hopelessness exactly.

clue.text: Club subscription covers 50 fights

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so the outer piece wraps the inner one

blocks.note: membership dues are a club's fee
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A boxing club's membership fee pays for fifty bouts.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside DUES, between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Duels are formal combats between two people, so particular kinds of fights.

clue.text: Followed and reached the top

blocks.note: first meaning: came after, as one monarch takes over from another
second meaning: achieved success

explanation.surface: Someone trailed behind a leader and then made it to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look like one story of a climber; they are separate meanings of one past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both taking a predecessor's place in sequence and attaining one's aim or prospering.

clue.text: Capone perhaps leaving one country for another

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of an Al
a country of the southern hemisphere

explanation.surface: A gangster flees one nation and settles in a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The AL removed is from the middle, AUSTR-AL-IA. 'Another' only works as a definition because 'country' is carried over from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a second nation, in central Europe, which is all the word 'another' (meaning another country) asks for.

clue.text: Doubt inaccurate tennis player could do this?

definitions.text: inaccurate tennis player could do this?

blocks.note: first meaning: a qualification or hesitation, as in accepting something without hesitation

blocks.clueFragment: inaccurate tennis player could do this?
blocks.note: second meaning: a player who faults may have to serve again

explanation.surface: We wonder whether a wayward tennis player might hesitate.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as RE- (again) plus SERVE; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting something with reservation or without reserve uses the word as a noun for doubt or qualification.

clue.text: Papa with uniform – right outfit for work

blocks.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the abbreviation for right
a suit is a matching outfit

explanation.surface: A father in uniform has the proper clothes for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing beside 'outfit', but it is only the letter U from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an occupation or activity someone engages in, so it can stand for a line of work.

clue.text: Forgives Conservative after former exploits

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the later piece is written second

blocks.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A Tory pardons misdeeds from someone's past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun meaning deeds, but it is the verb meaning makes use of.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to pardon or overlook it, a direct synonym for the verb forgive.

clue.text: Gets bigger screen, as I ordered

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone upgrades to a larger television, just as they requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' seems to mean bought, as in ordering a screen; it is the instruction to reorder the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to grow in size or amount, which is exactly what getting bigger describes.

clue.text: Naughty child not at first making mistake

indicators.note: 'not at first' means drop the opening letter, so the word loses its beginning

blocks.note: a little terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A misbehaving child initially doesn't get things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR loses its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straightforward synonym for something done incorrectly.

clue.text: Takes off the woman’s enthralling diamonds

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: the woman is she, so the woman's (she is) is she's
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A woman removes her dazzling diamond jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The woman's' reads as possessive, but it stands for SHE'S, a contraction of she is.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed clothing or skin is to remove or cast it off, just as one takes off a coat.

clue.text: Move to Tunisia for employment

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them around, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to North Africa to take up a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' looks like relocation, but it is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation, especially in old job advertisements ('situations vacant'), is a post or position of paid work.

clue.text: Nearest criminal aimed and hit me, not hard

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or wrong, so the letters are put out of order
'not' tells us to leave a letter out, so it is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A victim complains that the closest crook took aim and struck, though not forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is removed from AIMED HIT ME before the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate can mean closest in relation or position, as in one's immediate neighbour or immediate family.

clue.text: Former PM on river vessel

blocks.note: Theresa May was British Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019
a crossword favourite: a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: A retired prime minister takes a trip on a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the river after the PM in a down clue. The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower is a famous sailing ship, so it is an example of a vessel.

clue.text: Poorly Lucy exited, leaving university feverishly

indicators.note: poorly means badly or in poor shape, so the letters are jumbled
whatever is leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written, the fodder
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A sick student called Lucy walked out of college running a high temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: One U comes out of LUCY EXITED before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverishly here means in a state of agitated haste or nervous energy, which is how someone acts excitedly.

clue.text: Gets free garments after ends of the sales

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of each is kept
coming after something means following it, so the later piece is written second

blocks.note: final letter of the word
final letter of the word
capes are sleeveless cloaks

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up clothes for nothing once the sales finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends' takes the final letter of both 'the' and 'sales', not the two ends of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break loose from confinement, which is what someone who gets free does.

clue.text: Ammunition container for every ship

blocks.note: a clip holds cartridges for a gun
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Each ship in a fleet is issued with a box of ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For every' looks like a link phrase, but it supplies the letters PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipper is a fast sailing ship of the nineteenth century, famous in the tea trade.

clue.text: Rubbish student’s lost motivation

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: drivel is nonsense, talk that is rubbish
L for learner, as on the plates of a novice motorist

explanation.surface: A useless student has lost all enthusiasm for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student's lost' means the student is lost: the L comes off the end of DRIVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is energy and determination to achieve something, which is what motivation provides.

clue.text: First hammered nail – it supports cabinet, essentially

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order
the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder
the middle letter of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A carpenter drives in a nail before anything else, since it holds up the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in NAIL, IT and the central I of 'cabinet' together; 'supports' just puts the last piece with the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the beginning, so it is an adjective meaning first in order.

clue.text: Busy English artist turned up, scratching bottom

indicators.note: scratching out means deleting, and the bottom of a down entry is its last letter
in a down clue, turning something up flips it to read from the bottom

blocks.note: Eng is the abbreviation for English
Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: A busy English painter looks up, scratching his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom of a word is its end, so the final letter goes before the rest is flipped to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone line or a toilet that is engaged is occupied or in use, so busy.

clue.text: Somewhat machinating state

indicators.note: somewhat means to a degree, so only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: letters three to seven of the word

explanation.surface: A government that is a little bit scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb or a condition; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country, and a state can mean a nation with its own government.

clue.text: Person swallowing story, very trusting

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: a being is a living creature or person
a story can be a fib or lie
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone who swallows a tall tale is extremely gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowing a story' is the idiom for being taken in, which fits the definition neatly, but here 'swallowing' is a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Being believing means accepting what one is told, so having faith or being trusting.

clue.text: Sordid small stations

blocks.note: base means low or morally vile
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Seedy little railway stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stations' is a noun for military or operational posts, not train stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Bases are places where forces or staff are stationed, so they are military or research stations.

clue.text: We admit ignoring every other court order

indicators.note: ignoring every other letter skips alternate ones, so only every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to disregarding judicial instructions now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court order' looks like the whole definition, but 'court' supplies CT and only 'order' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree issued by an authority, so a formal order or command.

clue.text: Young dogs quietly finished pastry dishes

blocks.note: p for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
up means over, as in 'time's up'
pies are baked dishes in pastry

explanation.surface: Young dogs silently polish off some pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' reads as ate up, but it supplies UP in the sense of over.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppies are dogs in their first year, so the plural noun for young dogs.

clue.text: Drinking without husband complaining

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: wining is drinking wine, as in wining and dining
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife grumbles about drinking alone with no spouse there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, which would remove H; here it means outside, so WINING goes round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Whining is grumbling in a querulous, peevish way, so it is a synonym for complaining.

clue.text: Son photographs hares

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
prints are photographic copies

explanation.surface: A son takes pictures of wild hares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hares' looks like the animals, but it is a verb: runs very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run at great speed, like the animal, so it matches the verb meaning to dash flat out.

clue.text: Snake with tail cut departs disconcerted

indicators.note: cutting off a tail removes the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a rattler is a rattlesnake
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A snake whose tail has been chopped off slithers away upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A rattlesnake's tail is literally its rattle, which adds to the joke of cutting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattled is informal for flustered or unnerved, which matches disconcerted closely.
